REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4, u5
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u4
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved) -> u1
(u0, has_door_key & !blocker_moved) -> u5
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_door_key) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, door_open) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_picked_up) -> u4
(u3, else) -> u3
(u4, else) -> u4
(u5, else) -> u5
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved, u1) -> 0.1
(u0, has_door_key & !blocker_moved, u5) -> -1.0
(u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, door_open, u3) -> 0.1
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> 1.0
feedback: The RM is well-formed and faithful to the task. Format: all required headers present (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES with u4 declared in STATES and serving as the accepting state), transitions are predicate-only using & and !, and every state has an else self-loop so irrelevant events (notably key_lost, which this task does not involve) are absorbed without spurious progress. Semantic fidelity: the core constraint is enforced correctly — from u0, taking the key before the ball has been moved (has_door_key & !blocker_moved, which in u0 is equivalent to has_door_key since blocker_moved has not yet held) traps the machine in u5 with a -1.0 penalty and no further reward, exactly penalizing the key-first path the task forbids; the legal ordering ball-then-key-then-door-then-box progresses u0->u1->u2->u3->u4 with small bounded shaping rewards (0.1) and a terminal 1.0 at target_picked_up. Treating 'you have moved the ball away' as satisfied once blocker_moved has held (no regression needed on a later drop-back) is consistent with the task's wording, and the final state remains reachable only through task-compliant behavior since the u5 trap blocks any violator. Reachability: all six states are reachable and u4 is reachable via a physically valid plan (pick up ball, drop it aside, pick up key, toggle door, drop key, pick up box); the chain respects all environment constraints (door_open requires has_door_key, the box requires an open door, one object at a time). Reward safety: each reward fires at most once, no cycles emit reward, total is bounded (at most 1.3 on success, exactly -1.0 on violation), so there is no farming or hacking vector. Compactness is reasonable: the five-state mission chain mirrors the environment's forced ordering plus one dedicated trap state for the constraint, with no redundant states. Minor notes only: the guard at u0 could be simplified to has_door_key (blocker_moved is necessarily false in u0), and the RM silently tolerates dropping the ball back in front of the door after having moved it once — defensible under the 'until you have moved' reading, though a stricter current-state encoding with a u1 regression on !blocker_moved would penalize that path as well. Neither point rises to a rejection.

feedback: Accepted. The candidate defines exactly the five environment-declared propositions and no extras; none are missing, and `key_lost` is correctly defined even though the RM never references it. `has_door_key`, `door_open`, and `target_picked_up` match the documented expressions verbatim (carrying check with color-matched door scan; open-door scan; box carried with mission-string match via the dynamic `env.mission`, no fixed color assumed). `blocker_moved` is a semantically equivalent realization of the documented `not any(ball at (dx-1, dy))`: it scans for the door by type (valid, exactly one door) and tests its left neighbor cell, which is precisely the ball's documented start cell; the `x > 0` guard only prevents an out-of-bounds `grid.get(-1, y)` and never activates for the real door (dx >= 2 by layout). It correctly yields true while the ball is in hand (not on the grid), turns false again only if the ball is dropped back on that cell, and ignores balls elsewhere. `key_lost` implements the event `prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D` with K and D recomputed identically to the persistent functions, so it co-occurs with neither `has_door_key` nor `door_open`; the added `bool(env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'])` existence guard is a harmless defensive read that never changes the truth value since the previous valuation is guaranteed present and complete (all-false at step 0). It fires for exactly one step after the key is dropped while the door is closed, matching the example trace (step 19 drop with open door keeps it false). All five return proper booleans, use only documented API (`env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, `env.carrying`, `env.mission`, object `type`/`color`/`is_open`, read-only `previous_valuation`), guard empty cells with `is not None` before attribute access, and contain no imports, no actions, no mutations of the environment or episode memory. Syntax is valid and executable.
